title: ATP Handoff Artifact (Execution Receipt)
description: Canonical receipt schema written by a completing task (sub-agent or primary) and validated by the T2 receipt scan. Execution receipts are handoff artifacts — there is one schema, not two.

bundle_id.description: Canonical bundle correlation identifier assigned at dispatch.

protocol_id.description: ID of the protocol that produced this receipt. kebab-case, matches the protocol's frontmatter `id`.

receipt_sha256.description: SHA-256 of canonical receipt bytes with this field omitted. Required by the ledger before terminal completion.

next_package.description: Next bounded program package, or null when none is queued.

completed_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp marking when the task finished (successfully or not).

execution_phase_reached.description: The furthest ATP canonical phase reached before completion or halt. Matches the 6 phases defined in the root SPEC.md.

result.description: success=all phases completed including post-execution var updates. partial=execution completed but post-execution review missed or incomplete. failure=halted before or during execution.

changes.description: Structured list of state changes applied during execution. Empty array allowed for read-only or fully-idempotent tasks.

target.description: What the change applied to (file path, var id, endpoint, resource identifier).

summary.description: One-line human-readable description of the change.

var_updates.description: Variable IDs updated during post-execution review. Empty array if no vars changed.

next_action.description: What should happen next. none=task fully done, no follow-up. continue=additional work queued or expected. escalate=review authority or deployment owner intervention required.

state_after.description: Free-form snapshot of task-relevant state after execution. Keys are task-specific; T2 does not enforce structure here, only presence.

severity.description: Optional severity of the receipt itself when the task produced a notable outcome. Matches the ATP canonical severity vocabulary: info=awareness only, warn=recoverable issue, critical=halt-level. Absent when the task completed cleanly with no notable outcome.
